text.p: Roger Bailey tossed a five-hitter for his first career shutout as the Colorado Rockies posted a 4-0 victory over the Chicago Cubs, who set the all-time National League record for the worst start to a season on Wednesday.

The Cubs fell to 0-12 to break the 1884 Detroit Wolverines' all-time NL record for losses to start a season. They are a loss away from matching the second-worst start in modern history, set by the 1904 Washington Senators and 1920 Detroit Tigers. The major-league record of 0-21 was set by the Baltimore Orioles in 1988.

"Up til today we've played pretty good baseball, but today was a game where we just didn't do anything right," said Cubs manager Jim Riggleman. "The result was we made some mistakes and you end up losing the ballgame. That was as poorly played a ballgame as you can play at this level.

"It doesn't matter whether it's day, night, artificial turf or grass, we just need to play better baseball," added Riggleman. "I had thought we had been making progress up until today. If there's one game in this losing streak that embarrasses us, it's today."
In Atlanta, four pitchers combined on a three-hitter, and Kenny Lofton went 4-for-5 with a solo home run to lead the Atlanta Braves to a 7-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday.
The Braves extended their winning streak to five games. They scored 25 runs and banged out 40 hits in the three-game sweep of the Reds.

Left-hander Terrell Wade was the emergency starter for Greg Maddux, who was a late scratch with a sore right hamstring. Wade pitched 4-1/3 innings and allowed an unearned run and three hits. He walked none and struck out five.
Lofton had three singles and a stolen base to go with his home run. He has 21 hits in his last 37 at-bats.

At Florida, Pat Rapp and two relievers combined on a five-hitter and Gary Sheffield snapped a tie with a solo homer as the Florida Marlins ended a three-game losing streak with a 2-1 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals.
Rapp limited St. Louis to one run and four hits over six innings, walking two and striking out six. He has allowed just one run and nine hits over his last two starts, spanning 15 innings.
In Houston, Shane Reynolds pitched a three-hitter for his second straight complete game and drove in a pair of runs as the Houston Astros routed the Montreal Expos 10-2.
Reynolds (2-1) allowed two runs and struck out 10.

Jeff Bagwell and Bill Spiers each drove in two runs for the Astros, who have alternated losses and wins in their last eight games. Derek Bell, who entered the game batting just .192 (10-for-52), was 4-for-5 with a run and an RBI.

In New York, Pedro Astacio pitched no-hit ball for seven-plus innings and Wilton Guerrero and Eric Karros belted two-run homers as the Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the New York Mets 5-2 to split their two-game series.
Brett Butler added five hits -- all singles -- for Los Angeles.
In the eighth, Astacio hung a 1-0 breaking pitch to leadoff hitter Carlos Baerga, who laced it down the right-field line to end the no-hit bid.
"I noticed that I had a no-hitter," he said. "Nobody (on the bench) said anything. But when I walked on the field, fans were yelling, Pedro, you've got a no-hitter,'."

In Philadelphia, Glenallen Hill homered twice and drove in the go-ahead run in the top of the 10th inning as the San Francisco Giants won their sixth straight game, edging the Philadelphia Phillies, 6-5.
The Giants, off to their best start since 1987 at 10-3, were the beneficiary of three straight walks by Reggie Harris (0-1) to open the 10th.
Hill hit a groundball that third baseman Scott Rolen threw away, allowing the go-ahead run to score. Bill Mueller followed with a sacrifice fly, bringing home a much-needed insurance run.
In Pittsburgh, Tony Gwynn had three hits, including a solo homer, leading the San Diego Padres to their third win in four games, 7-5 over the Pittsburgh Pirates.

Gwynn's two-out solo shot off starter Steve Cooke in the top of the first inning put San Diego ahead to stay and the Padres added five runs in the fifth. They held on to break a three-game losing streak against Pittsburgh.
Gwynn has three homers in 54 at-bats this season after hitting three in 451 at-bats last season.
"I've seen him so long he just continues to amaze me," Padres manager Bruce Bochy said. "He's gonna go down as one of the greatest hitters of all time."
